title: Which Reserves Count as Standing on a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Which reserves count as standing on a Keyturn Host Payout Account turns on whether money has lately been freed and on whether a reserve has lately been taken.

| Reserves freed in the month up to that day | Reserves taken in that month | What counts as standing |
|---|---|---|
| One or more | Any | Every reserve ever taken on the account less every reserve ever freed from it |
| None | One or more | The reserves taken in the twelve months up to that day less the reserves freed in that same period |
| None | None | The reserves taken in the month up to that day less the reserves freed in that month |

Whichever stretch is measured, the reserve standing is rounded half to even to two decimal places and is never less than nothing, because freeing more in a period than was taken in it leaves the account holding nothing back rather than owing the host more than it holds.

## Points of judgement

**A reserve has been freed this month.** The first row governs whatever else the month shows, and the whole history of the account is taken.

**Nothing freed this month but a reserve taken in it.** The second row governs and the stretch is the twelve months up to that day, on both sides of the subtraction.

**Neither freed nor taken this month.** The third row governs and the stretch is the month up to that day.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account on which reserves of 2000.00 USD have been taken over its whole life and 900.00 USD freed over that life; 1500.00 USD taken and 700.00 USD freed in the twelve months up to that day; and 400.00 USD taken and nothing freed in the month up to that day. The reserve standing is 1100.00 USD in the first row, 800.00 USD in the second and 400.00 USD in the third.
